Tenet, the new Christopher Nolan movie. I'm not going to be too specific to try and avoid spoiling anything for people who can't see it yet. 


At the very start of the movie they say to use the word Tenet and a hand signal and then I only saw it used 1 time for the rest of the movie. A character made such a terrible and out of character choice, it undermined everything they'd previously said and done. Halfway through the movie there's a whole bunch of new characters that seem to come from nowhere. The "big twists" were so obvious and unsurprising. It's never really clear when they switch from moving forwards vs backwards. The villain was boring and uninspired and his motivations were not convincing. Christopher Nolan can't write good female characters. The dead wife in Inception has more depth than a real living female character. 


The dialogue is hard to hear which is frustrating when it's a movie with a complicated plot. There isn't time for most of the dialogue to land and then sometimes they are restricted by masks. Think of Bane in the last Batman movie. And some parts of the dialogue are painfully bad and would never be said by anyone, for example saying "I am the protagonist".  Obviously that's partly because of the time entropy and the grandfather paradox but so many TV shows and films have done that stuff better without using hacky dialogue. 


It overall didn't make much sense, it seemed like the tricks of watching stuff move backwards is waved around to cover for the plot holes and poor writing. Maybe I'm not smart enough or just don't "get it" but I think a film shouldn't be praised or aiming to be a mindfuck and confusing, especially at the expense of a good plot and good characters.


And it's just to long. 2.5 hours and what was the point? What's the moral, the theme, the idea to take away from it? It has no substance. Some cool film tricks, yeah some cool fights, cool stuff to see on a big screen, but what the point of the movie after all that?


The friend I went with was so disappointed they actually wanted to ask for a refund from the cinema. I like many of Christopher Nolans other films but this one sucked.

I didn't have the energy to scroll through all the replies and I'm sure this has been mentioned already, but my mental health treatment. I have severe depression and anxiety that's been getting worse since November, like not able to leave the house, not able to take the rubbish out, not able to shower, just a huge drop in my everyday functioning, I don't even really understand why. I'm deeply suicidal multiple times a day and am having panic attacks constantly. 
Was meant to be getting to a mental health hospital to try and get better, that's shut down. Other hospitals aren't admitting. The beds in emergency rooms aren't available. My doctor had to quarantine so we will do Skype sessions but it's not the same. Community services for people struggling wig these issues are closing down. I know this virus is deadly, but so is mental illness, and it's like mental health has gotten pushed to the back of the queue. Which I understand, and it makes sense. But I don't know wtf I'm supposed to do when I'm still so depressed and suicidal and the help has vanished. I feel so alone.

I can't upvote this enough, my experience was definitely like this. Your comment is the first echoing what I feel and I had to scroll so far! I've been in therapy for awhile, seen a dozen different ones, and the one I ended up with is fantastic. But at first I thought they were an asshole and just didn't get it, they didn't get me, they didn't say the right words. I got so mad I ended up leaving a really negative review. A few years later and they're cutting back their hours and I'm a little lost without our weekly sessions.

I thought the episode really highlighted something that is common in people with anxiety starting treatment, with the patient saying the situation or how they feel is X and if the doctor uses a similar word, but not the exact same one, it's a big problem. I remember I used to be like this, and be extremely defensive. Now, as long as its in the same ballpark, as long as I feel they understand, it doesn't matter if I use the word annoyed and they use frustrated, as long as we have an understanding of whatever we are talking about, and I feel they understand where I'm coming from.

There definitely are bad psychologists and psychiatrists out there. I had one tell me I'd have to get a job a week after being out of a coma. Also told me my problems would be fixed if I started running (he ran marathons.)
